title: Exodus Chapter 38 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Exodus chapter 38 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Exodus Chapter 38 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Exodus Chapter 38.

questions.question: What material was used to make the altar of burnt offering?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:1 states that the altar of burnt offering was made of shittim wood.

questions.question: How high was the altar of burnt offering made?
questions.explanation: According to Exodus 38:1, the altar was three cubits high.

questions.question: Where were the horns placed on the altar?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:2 says the horns were made on the four corners of the altar.

questions.question: What was the altar overlaid with?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:2 mentions that the altar was overlaid with brass.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT listed as a vessel made for the altar?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:3 lists pots, shovels, basons (basins), fleshhooks, and firepans, but not bowls.

questions.question: What material were all the vessels of the altar made from?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:3 states that all the vessels of the altar were made of brass.

questions.question: What was made under the compass of the altar?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:4 specifies that a brasen grate of network was made under the compass of the altar.

questions.question: How many rings were cast for the ends of the grate of brass?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:5 mentions that four rings were cast for the four ends of the grate of brass.

questions.question: What was used to make the staves for the altar?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:6 states the staves were made of shittim wood and overlaid with brass.

questions.question: True or False: The altar was made solid and not hollow.
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:7 clearly states that the altar was made hollow with boards.

questions.question: What was the laver made of?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:8 says that the laver and its foot were made of brass.

questions.question: From what were the looking glasses, used for the laver, made?
options: From the women assembling at the tabernacle door
From the gold of the sanctuary
questions.correctAnswer: From the women assembling at the tabernacle door
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:8 states the looking glasses were made from the women assembling at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.

questions.question: True or False: The hangings on the south side of the court were made of fine twined linen and measured one hundred cubits.
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:9 confirms the south side hangings were fine twined linen and were one hundred cubits long.

questions.question: How many pillars were there on the south side of the court?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:10 states there were twenty pillars on the south side.

questions.question: True or False: The hooks of the pillars on the north side of the court were made of bronze.
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:11 states the hooks of the pillars and their fillets were of silver, not bronze.

medium.title: Exodus Chapter 38 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Exodus Chapter 38 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What material were the hangings of the court made from according to Exodus 38?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:16 states that all the hangings of the court round about were of fine twined linen, emphasizing the importance of purity and holiness in the tabernacle's design.

questions.question: How many pillars were set on the west side of the court?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:12 mentions that on the west side there were hangings of fifty cubits with ten pillars and ten sockets, showing the careful structural planning of the tabernacle court.

questions.question: What does the use of silver hooks and fillets on the pillars teach about Christian character?
options: The value of integrity and beautifying God’s work
questions.correctAnswer: The value of integrity and beautifying God’s work
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:10, 17 show that the hooks of the pillars and their fillets were of silver, symbolizing that Christian service should be done with integrity and care to honor God’s holiness and beauty.

questions.question: According to Exodus 38, what was the height in breadth of the gate's hanging?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:18 states the height in breadth of the gate's hanging was five cubits, matching the hangings of the court, demonstrating the harmony and order in God’s design.

questions.question: What purpose do the brass sockets and silver hooks serve in the construction of the tabernacle court?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:17 describes sockets of brass and hooks of silver for the pillars, indicating the practical need for stability combined with the spiritual principle of honoring God with beauty.

questions.question: How does the description of the court’s gate made with needlework colors (blue, purple, scarlet) teach about humility and reverence in worship?
options: It shows the sacredness and reverence due to approaching God
It emphasizes human creativity over God’s instructions
It encourages lavish displays to impress others
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the sacredness and reverence due to approaching God
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:18 highlights the needlework of blue, purple, and scarlet, colors often associated with royalty and priesthood, teaching believers to approach God with humility and reverence.

questions.question: True or False: The pins of the tabernacle and the court round about were made of silver.
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:20 specifies that all the pins of the tabernacle and the court round about were of brass, not silver, reflecting the use of durable materials for foundational purposes.

questions.question: Who was responsible for making all that the LORD commanded Moses concerning the tabernacle?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:22 states that Bezaleel son of Uri, from the tribe of Judah, made all that the LORD commanded Moses, showing God’s provision of gifted craftsmen for His work.

questions.question: What does the involvement of Aholiab as an engraver and embroiderer teach Christians about using their talents?
options: Believers should use their skills to serve God’s purposes
Skills are only useful for personal gain
Artistic talents are unimportant in worship
Only priests should serve in the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should use their skills to serve God’s purposes
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:23 describes Aholiab as an engraver and embroiderer who worked on the tabernacle, illustrating that all believers are called to use their gifts in service to God and community.

questions.question: Based on Exodus 38:21, what does the careful counting and service of the Levites indicate about Christian obedience?
options: Obedience involves faithful service according to God’s commands
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience involves faithful service according to God’s commands
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:21 emphasizes the counting of the tabernacle and service of the Levites according to Moses' command, teaching that obedience includes faithfully fulfilling God’s instructions in ministry.

questions.question: What lesson about generosity can be drawn from the half-shekel offering described in Exodus 38:26?
options: Each person contributed equally to support God’s work
Only the wealthy gave to the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: Each person contributed equally to support God’s work
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:25-26 describes a half-shekel offering from each person, emphasizing that God values equal, willing contributions from all for His purposes, encouraging generosity in the community.

questions.question: True or False: The sockets for the pillars and the vail were cast from the hundred talents of silver given by the congregation.
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:27 confirms that the hundred talents of silver were cast into sockets of the sanctuary and the vail, demonstrating the use of offerings directly for God’s holy work.

questions.question: Which of the following items was NOT made from brass according to Exodus 38?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:3 and 38:8 mention brass for altar vessels and laver; 38:20 mentions pins of brass; 38:10 and 38:17 specify hooks of silver, showing differentiation in materials for function and beauty.

questions.question: What biblical virtue is taught by the detailed and careful construction of the tabernacle court described in Exodus 38:12-20?
questions.explanation: The precise measurements and materials for pillars, sockets, hooks, and hangings in Exodus 38:12-20 illustrate the virtue of faithfulness and reverence in serving God, honoring His holiness through obedient workmanship.

questions.question: True or False: The court gate hangings on each side were fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three sockets each.
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:14-15 describe the court gate hangings on both sides as fifteen cubits with three pillars and three sockets, showing symmetry and order in God’s design.

hard.title: Exodus Chapter 38 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Exodus Chapter 38.

questions.question: Who assisted Bezaleel in the construction of the tabernacle, as an engraver and embroiderer?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:23 states that Aholiab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, was an engraver and a cunning workman assisting Bezaleel.

questions.question: How much gold, in talents and shekels, was used for all the work of the holy place?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:24 specifies that all the gold used in the holy place's construction, including the offering, totaled 29 talents and 730 shekels.

questions.question: What was the amount of silver contributed by those numbered in the congregation?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:25 reports that the silver contributed by the congregation was 100 talents and 1715 shekels.

questions.question: What was the specific amount each man gave as a silver offering according to the shekel of the sanctuary?
options: A bekah, which is half a shekel
questions.correctAnswer: A bekah, which is half a shekel
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:26 explains that every man gave a bekah, equivalent to half a shekel, as an offering for the sanctuary.

questions.question: What was made from the hundred talents of silver according to Exodus 38?
options: The sockets of the sanctuary and the vail
The brasen altar and its vessels
questions.correctAnswer: The sockets of the sanctuary and the vail
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:27 states that the hundred talents of silver were used to cast the sockets of the sanctuary and the vail.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'bekah' mentioned in Exodus 38:26 in relation to biblical typology?
options: It typifies the ransom price for redemption, as later referenced in Exodus 30:13
It represents the full price of atonement in Leviticus
It symbolizes the tithe given to the Levites
It is the price for a slave in Deuteronomy
questions.correctAnswer: It typifies the ransom price for redemption, as later referenced in Exodus 30:13
questions.explanation: The 'bekah' or half-shekel in Exodus 38:26 corresponds to Exodus 30:13, where it is called a ransom price to the LORD, symbolizing redemption.

questions.question: Which materials were used to overlay the staves made of shittim wood for the altar?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:6 clarifies that the staves made of shittim wood were overlaid with brass.

questions.question: True or False: The hangings of the court were made of fine twined linen all around the court.
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:16 confirms that all the hangings of the court round about were of fine twined linen.

questions.question: What was the primary color scheme used in the needlework for the gate of the court?
options: Blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen
Purple, crimson, gold, and fine wool
questions.correctAnswer: Blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:18 describes the gate's needlework hangings as incorporating blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen.

questions.question: How many men were numbered from twenty years old and upward, according to the census used in Exodus 38?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:26 records the total as six hundred thousand three thousand five hundred fifty men counted from twenty years old and upward.

questions.question: Which tribe did Bezaleel, the chief craftsman of the tabernacle's work, belong to?
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:22 states that Bezaleel was the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the detailed enumeration of materials and craftsmen in Exodus 38, reflecting completeness and order?
questions.explanation: The chapter's detailed listing of materials and craftsmen serves as an inclusio, framing the work to emphasize completeness and sacred order (Exodus 38:21-31).

questions.question: What was made from the brass offering amounting to seventy talents and 2,400 shekels?
options: Sockets to the door of the tabernacle, the brasen altar, grate, and altar vessels
questions.correctAnswer: Sockets to the door of the tabernacle, the brasen altar, grate, and altar vessels
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:29-30 explains that the brass offering was used to make sockets for the door, brasen altar, grate, and vessels of the altar.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage does the half-shekel offering in Exodus 38:26 echo in its function as a ransom or atonement price?
questions.explanation: Exodus 30:13 also commands a half-shekel as a ransom price to the LORD, echoing the offering described in Exodus 38:26.

questions.question: True or False: The hooks of the pillars and their fillets around the court were made of brass.
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:17 specifies that the hooks of the pillars and their fillets were made of silver, not brass.

theological.title: Exodus Chapter 38 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Exodus Chapter 38 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the significance of the altar's dimensions and materials described in Exodus 38:1-2 in revealing God's holiness and justice?
options: The altar's brass overlay and precise measurements symbolize God's unchanging holiness and just judgment
The altar's size shows God's indifference to human worship
The altar's wood indicates God's preference for natural elements only
The horns on the altar represent human power over God
questions.correctAnswer: The altar's brass overlay and precise measurements symbolize God's unchanging holiness and just judgment
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:1-2 describes the altar made of shittim wood overlaid with brass and its exact dimensions, emphasizing God's holiness and justice through the altar's durable and measured design. Brass often symbolizes judgment (Exodus 38:1-2).

questions.question: According to Exodus 38:8, what does the laver made from the women’s looking glasses symbolize in the context of sanctification?
options: The laver symbolizes purification and the communal participation in holiness
It represents God's wrath against vanity
It is a symbol of wealth and status
It shows the futility of human effort for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: The laver symbolizes purification and the communal participation in holiness
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:8 states the laver was made of brass from the women’s looking glasses, symbolizing the community’s collective role in sanctification and the need for purification before approaching God.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the detailed description of the court’s hangings, pillars, and sockets in Exodus 38:9-17?
options: The doctrine of God's transcendence and the separation between the holy and the profane
The doctrine of justification by faith alone
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's transcendence and the separation between the holy and the profane
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:9-17 describes the court’s boundaries with fine linen hangings and metal sockets, illustrating God's transcendence and the necessary separation of the sacred space from the common world, a key element of holiness (Lev 10:3).

questions.question: How does Exodus 38:22-23 reveal the attribute of God's wisdom in the work of Bezaleel and Aholiab?
options: God imparts wisdom and skill to chosen individuals for His redemptive purposes
God emphasizes human strength over divine guidance
God's wisdom is limited to the priesthood alone
God delegates all creative work without involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God imparts wisdom and skill to chosen individuals for His redemptive purposes
questions.explanation: Verses 22-23 highlight that Bezaleel and Aholiab were endowed by God with artistic skills and wisdom, demonstrating God's attribute as the giver of wisdom for His redemptive work (Exodus 31:3).

questions.question: What does the use of specific materials such as gold, silver, and brass in Exodus 38:24-31 teach about God's holiness and the nature of worship?
options: God requires offerings of precious and durable materials symbolizing purity and judgment
God prefers only humble, simple materials for worship
Material wealth is a measure of divine favor
Only gold is acceptable for worship
questions.correctAnswer: God requires offerings of precious and durable materials symbolizing purity and judgment
questions.explanation: The passage lists gold, silver, and brass used for the sanctuary vessels, indicating that worship demands offerings of the finest and most symbolic materials, reflecting God's holiness, purity, and judgment (Exodus 38:24-31).

questions.question: How do the horns on the altar described in Exodus 38:2 serve as a foreshadowing of Christ's redemptive work?
options: They symbolize the power of atonement and refuge found in Christ’s sacrifice
They represent the strength of Israel's military conquest
They symbolize human authority over sin
They represent the temple priests' dominance
questions.correctAnswer: They symbolize the power of atonement and refuge found in Christ’s sacrifice
questions.explanation: The horns on the altar (Exodus 38:2) symbolized a place of refuge and power in atonement, foreshadowing Christ’s ultimate sacrifice providing salvation and protection (Hebrews 13:10-12).

questions.question: Sceptics claim the detailed measurements and materials in Exodus 38 are merely ritualistic and lack theological meaning. What does Exodus 38:1-20 actually teach about the significance of these details?
options: These details symbolize divine order, holiness, and the structured approach to worshiping a holy God
These details are arbitrary and have no deeper meaning
The measurements only serve architectural purposes
The materials reflect economic status, not theology
questions.correctAnswer: These details symbolize divine order, holiness, and the structured approach to worshiping a holy God
questions.explanation: Exodus 38:1-20 shows detailed measurements and materials that reflect God's character and holiness, emphasizing the importance of order and reverence in worship (1 Corinthians 14:40).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Exodus 38:26 and 38:27 provide about God's provision and community responsibility?
options: God requires a communal offering, symbolizing unity and equal responsibility in worship
Only priests are responsible for worship provision
Generosity is optional in the covenant community
questions.correctAnswer: God requires a communal offering, symbolizing unity and equal responsibility in worship
questions.explanation: Verse 26 states each man paid half a shekel, and verse 27 describes the use of this silver for sockets, revealing God's design for communal responsibility and unity in worship provision.

questions.question: How does Exodus 38:18-19 demonstrate the attribute of God's beauty and majesty in His covenant dwelling?
options: The intricate needlework and vibrant colors reflect God's majestic and beautiful presence
The gate's size shows God's indifference to aesthetics
God's beauty is irrelevant to worship
questions.correctAnswer: The intricate needlework and vibrant colors reflect God's majestic and beautiful presence
questions.explanation: The gate's embroidery of blue, purple, and scarlet linen (Exodus 38:18-19) reflects God’s attribute of beauty and majesty in His holy dwelling, signifying His glorious presence.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Exodus 38:21-23 provide in the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: The skilled artisans enable the construction of a sanctuary pointing to God’s presence among His people, prefiguring Christ’s incarnation
It shows human independence from God
It reveals the failure of Israel's worship
It describes the fall of man
questions.correctAnswer: The skilled artisans enable the construction of a sanctuary pointing to God’s presence among His people, prefiguring Christ’s incarnation
questions.explanation: Verses 21-23 describe craftsmen empowered by God to build the tabernacle, symbolizing God dwelling with His people, a theme fulfilled in Christ (John 1:14).

questions.question: What synthesis of doctrine emerges from Exodus 38:4-7 and 38:30 regarding the altar's design and its typological significance?
options: The altar’s design with a grate and hollow boards typifies Christ’s sacrifice and intercession
The design shows the temple's architectural innovation only
questions.correctAnswer: The altar’s design with a grate and hollow boards typifies Christ’s sacrifice and intercession
questions.explanation: Verses 4-7 describe the altar's grate and hollow design, while verse 30 emphasizes the bronze components, together symbolizing Christ’s sacrificial death and ongoing intercession (Hebrews 7:25).

questions.question: How does the description of the court’s pillars and sockets in Exodus 38:17 reveal God's attribute of faithfulness in maintaining the covenant?
options: The durable materials and secure pillars symbolize God's steadfastness in upholding His covenant
They show God's indifference to His promises
They reflect human weakness in worship
questions.correctAnswer: The durable materials and secure pillars symbolize God's steadfastness in upholding His covenant
questions.explanation: Verse 17 highlights silver fillets and brass sockets, symbolizing God’s faithfulness and the secure foundation of His covenant promises (Psalm 89:34).

questions.question: Which doctrinal truth is conveyed by the repeated emphasis on the use of brass for the altar, its vessels, and the court’s pins in Exodus 38:3, 6, 20, and 29-31?
options: Brass symbolizes judgment and purification, illustrating God's holiness demanding atonement
Brass shows human creativity without divine influence
Brass is used for decoration only
questions.correctAnswer: Brass symbolizes judgment and purification, illustrating God's holiness demanding atonement
questions.explanation: Brass is repeatedly used for the altar and its vessels (Exodus 38:3,6,20,29-31), signifying judgment and purification consistent with God's holy standards (Exodus 27:1-2).

questions.question: What theological insight arises from combining Exodus 38:9-10 and 38:14-15 about the structure and purpose of the tabernacle court?
options: The court’s design with pillars and hangings represents God’s provision of order and access to His presence
The court symbolizes exclusion from God
The court is purely functional without spiritual significance
The court shows human dominance over God
questions.correctAnswer: The court’s design with pillars and hangings represents God’s provision of order and access to His presence
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 and 14-15 describe the court’s hangings and pillars, indicating God’s orderly provision for worship and controlled access to His presence (Hebrews 9:8).

questions.question: How does Exodus 38:21-22 affirm the doctrine of divine sovereignty in the execution of God’s commands for the tabernacle?
options: God sovereignly appoints leaders and artisans to fulfill His redemptive plan
Humans act independently of God’s will
The people choose their own leaders
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly appoints leaders and artisans to fulfill His redemptive plan
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 show that the work was done under Moses’ command and by God-chosen artisans, demonstrating divine sovereignty in the fulfillment of His redemptive instructions.
